# Big-tech partner programs

<!-- Generated by scripts/partner-programs.mjs from data/partner-programs.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Nearly every partnership three.ws has today started with one question: *does this company have a partner program?* This page asks that question of the largest technology companies, all at once, and keeps the answers. It lists every partner program, startup program, marketplace, directory, grant, and recognition route a company like ours can join, ranks them, says exactly what to do next, and records every submission we make and every benefit we hold.

It is the wide net. The narrower docs stay authoritative for what they cover: [partners.md](../partners.md) is what each live partnership **is** and how to describe it, [opportunities.md](./opportunities.md) is the stuck-item pipeline, [prospects.md](./prospects.md) scores the 3D and avatar ecosystem, and the [listings registry](../listings-registry.md) tracks directories and awesome-lists.

Sibling pages: [ai company partner programs](./ai-programs.md), [motion partner programs](./motion-programs.md), and [who promotes partners](./promotion-programs.md) across every sector.

**166 programs across 46 companies.** 13 member / live, 1 submitted, waiting, 10 in progress, 16 ready, one human step, 81 eligible, not started, 33 verify fit first, 2 decided not to pursue, 3 not eligible, 7 retired or closed. We hold at least one membership at 8 of the 46 companies, and 58 of the open programs offer some form of promotion. Last full research sweep: 2026-11-06.

## Using this page

```sh
npm run programs:next -- --sector big-tech   # the ranked next actions, top 15
npm run programs:due -- --sector big-tech    # deadlines and expiring benefits in the next 30 days, submissions to chase
npm run programs:promo -- blog --sector big-tech   # programs that will promote us, by type
npm run programs -- --log <id> --action "Submitted the application" --status submitted --ref <url>
npm run programs -- --benefit <id> --name "Cloud credits" --value "USD 25,000" --state received --received 2026-11-06 --expires 2027-11-06
npm run programs:build                    # regenerate this page after editing data/partner-programs.json by hand
```

`--log` and `--benefit` update [data/partner-programs.json](../../data/partner-programs.json) and rebuild this page in one step. Log every submission the day it happens, with the confirmation link or email subject as `--ref`; log every benefit the day it lands, with its expiry. That is the whole tracking discipline.

**Scores** use the same F·R·A scale as [prospects.md](./prospects.md#how-a-prospect-is-scored): **F**it (5 = already in our code), **R**each (5 = millions of the right users or buyers), **A**ccess (5 = self-serve form, 1 = no public route), summed to 3-15.

## The plan

Every active program sits in exactly one wave. Work the waves in order; inside a wave, work top to bottom (highest score first). A program moves waves only when its status changes, so updating status is how the plan stays current.

## Who promotes partners

The open programs on this page that will put three.ws in front of their audience: co-marketing, social posts, blog posts, case studies, newsletters, featured placement, events, podcasts, press, or a partner badge. Ranked by promotion value: the program score plus two points for each kind of promotion one ask earns. Ask for the promotion in the same message as the application; it is far easier to get on the way in than after. The cross-sector view is [promotion-programs.md](./promotion-programs.md).

- **Google for Startups Cloud Program (Web3 tier).** We already hold Google Cloud for Web3 Startups credits and run on Cloud Run and Vertex AI, so this is mostly an upgrade path; funded tiers need VC backing we lack.
- **Chrome Web Store.** Both browser extensions (Walk Avatar and Checkout Companion) are built under extensions/ with a release checklist, so this is a submission, not a build. The same packages feed Edge Add-ons.
- **Google Cloud Marketplace and Agent Finder.** We run on Google Cloud, our MCP server is live, and the A2A agent card Agent Finder reads is already served at /.well-known/agent-card.json. The gate is Partner Network enrolment and the Marketplace vendor agreement, not engineering.
- **Google Cloud Partner Network.** Required plumbing for the Marketplace and Agent Finder listing; low standalone value until we have customer outcomes.
- **Google for Startups Gemini program.** We use Vertex Gemini and Imagen, so Gemini credits directly offset real spend.
- **Kaggle / Google DeepMind hackathons.** Good showcase for a Gemma/Gemini-driven 3D agent; none currently open.
- **Google Play (Android XR) publishing.** A Trusted Web Activity or native XR viewer for our avatars is possible but not on the current roadmap.
- **Google for Startups Accelerator (AI First / AI for Energy, North America).** Equity-free and US-based suits us, but we likely lack revenue and the 2026 track was energy only; watch for a 2027 AI First call.
- **Android XR Developer Catalyst Program.** Our AR/3D avatar stack could port to glasses, but this round is closed and engine support is Unity/Unreal/Godot, not WebXR.
- **Google Developer Experts (GDE).** The owner could qualify personally through Three.js/WebGL, MCP and Gemini content, but there is no self-serve route. Individual recognition for the owner, not the company.

- **Microsoft MCP server certification (Copilot Studio, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Foundry).** The legacy submission route closed 2026-10-31, so the package goes through the new Partner Center flow.
- **Microsoft Teams Store.** A Teams tab or message extension that previews GLBs is feasible; modest priority behind the Copilot Agent Store.
- **Visual Studio Marketplace (VS Code extensions).** The extensions are built in packages/ and not yet published.
- **Microsoft Store (Windows app, MSIX).** The installable web app packages through PWABuilder; listing copy is written.
- **Power Platform connector certification.** Five actions with OAuth and PKCE are built in the repo.
- **Microsoft Edge Add-ons.** Both extensions are built; listing copy is written and avoids partner-tier claims.
- **Microsoft ISV Success.** We already have a Marketplace publisher account, so this is the natural next enrolment.
- **Microsoft for Startups Founders Hub.** Useful as small Azure credit for Foundry model access, but large tiers need a VC; we are on GCP.
- **Microsoft MVP Award.** Our stack is not Microsoft-centric, so a nomination is a long shot. Individual recognition for the owner, not the company.

## Keeping it true

- **Never set `member` without proof**: an acceptance email, a portal that shows the membership, or a live listing. Record the proof as a `--log` entry with `--ref`.
- **Never upgrade a designation.** Program names and tiers are quoted exactly as the partner writes them; the framing rules in [partners.md](../partners.md#what-the-page-does-not-claim) apply here too.
- **Log the day it happens.** A submission that is not logged did not happen as far as the next person is concerned, and they will submit it again.
- **Re-sweep quarterly.** Programs get renamed, folded, and retired every few months. When a page 404s or redirects, set `closed` with the reason and the date so nobody re-researches it.
- **A new membership** also needs a card on `/partners` and `/partners/benefits` and a row in [partners.md](../partners.md) (see [partner-benefits.md](../partner-benefits.md#editing-rules)).
